NDT training in Amarillo, TX: how it works

Short answer: Amarillo technicians work through NDT theory at their own pace on the Atlantis portal, with written answers from an ASNT NDT Level III, and take the hands-on practical at their employer's facility under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Amarillo. Courses at Level 1, 2 and 3 cover UT, RT, MT, PT and VT year-round, and access is immediate once you enroll. We reply within one business day.

Amarillo is the commercial center of the Texas Panhandle, and the industries around it are spread across a very large map. Natural gas has been produced in the Panhandle for generations, and gathering lines, processing plants, compressor stations and transmission pipelines still crisscross the region. Refineries operate north of the city at Sunray, where Valero runs the McKee refinery, and at Borger. Wind farms now cover large stretches of the high plains, each tower a welded steel structure with bolted flanges that need periodic inspection.

The city also has a manufacturing and federal side. Bell's Amarillo Assembly Center handles assembly and modification work on military tiltrotor and helicopter programs, and the National Nuclear Security Administration's Pantex Plant sits northeast of town. Feedyards, meat processing, grain handling and fertilizer storage add pressure vessels, ammonia tanks and refrigeration piping to the inspection mix.

For a technician, that means variety and travel. A Panhandle inspector might shoot pipeline welds one week, gauge wall thickness at a gas plant the next and climb a wind tower after that. To discuss your situation, ask about NDT training in Amarillo.

How to get NDT certified in Amarillo: the SNT-TC-1A path step by step

Texas licenses radiographers, but it does not license UT, MT, PT or VT technicians. For those methods, what counts is certification under an employer's written practice, and under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer is the one that certifies. The usual path:

  1. Learn the employer's rules. Each written practice sets methods, levels, training and experience hours, examinations and vision checks. Pipeline contractors, plant inspection companies and fabricators around Amarillo do not all use the same one.
  2. Finish the formal training. Atlantis theory is self-paced online, which helps technicians who spend weeks on the road. The training-requirements matrix shows SNT-TC-1A recommended hours.
  3. Collect documented experience under a certified Level II or III, recording dates, methods, techniques and the jobs you worked on.
  4. Pass a vision examination for near acuity and color contrast at the interval the written practice requires.
  5. Pass the general examination on the theory of the method.
  6. Pass the specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment and the codes its clients use.
  7. Pass the practical examination on actual specimens, graded by a Level III or an examiner working under one.
  8. Get certified by the employer, and recertify on the interval in the written practice.

Pipeline operators add operator qualification and contractor prequalification on top, and the employer handles those. Check your starting point with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker and browse the NDT training FAQ. ASNT central certification (ASNT 9712 for Level I and II, ASNT NDT Level III beyond that) is the alternative route, and Atlantis prepares candidates for it.

Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3 NDT courses for Amarillo technicians

MethodWhat the course coversWhere it is used around Amarillo
UT (ultrasonic testing)Ultrasound physics, calibration, thickness measurement, straight-beam and angle-beam weld examination, reportingWall-thickness checks at gas plants, compressor stations and refineries; weld examination on piping, vessels and wind tower flanges
RT (radiographic testing)Exposure calculations, image quality indicators, film and digital imaging, weld interpretationPipeline girth welds and plant piping welds where the code or operator calls for radiography
MT (magnetic particle testing)Magnetizing methods, field direction, visible and fluorescent particles, demagnetization, evaluationStructural and tower welds, pressure equipment, lifting gear, rotating equipment parts
PT (liquid penetrant testing)Cleaning, penetrant application, dwell, removal, developing, interpreting indicationsStainless piping in processing plants, non-magnetic components, weld repairs
VT (visual testing)Weld visual criteria, measuring tools, lighting, remote viewing, documentationPipeline and plant welds, tower and structural steel, tank and vessel inspections
Level IIIASNT Basic and Method exam preparation, procedure writing, written practice administrationInspection contractors that need Level III oversight for client audits and prequalification

Beginners should look at NDT Level 1 training, experienced technicians at NDT Level 2 training, and program owners at ASNT Level III training. Pipeline and fabrication work also creates demand for certified welding inspectors; Atlantis runs a six-day AWS CWI exam-prep course online, one-to-one or at the employer's facility, and AWS administers the exam itself.

Ultrasonic testing (UT) training in Amarillo: pipelines, gas plants and wind towers

Across the Panhandle, ultrasonic testing does the heaviest lifting. Gas processing plants, compressor stations and refineries track corrosion with thickness readings, and the UT technician has to deliver numbers an engineer can trust: correct calibration, the right probe, attention to temperature and coatings, and readings taken at the same points each time. The UT course covers those basics and then moves to angle-beam weld examination, including beam angle choice, sensitivity setting, scan coverage and reflector sizing.

Wind energy adds a newer kind of UT work. Tower flange and shell welds, bolting and foundation hardware are examined during construction and maintenance, often under the owner's or turbine manufacturer's inspection plan, and the work is done at height with fall protection. Technicians who combine UT and MT are useful on those crews.

Pipeline construction still leans on radiography for girth welds, though automated ultrasonic systems are used on some projects as a specialist technique. A strong conventional UT foundation is the starting point for either path. Begin with ultrasonic testing training and practice with the UT Level 2 practice questions.

Where NDT technicians work around Amarillo

Natural gas and pipelines. Gathering systems, gas processing plants, compressor stations and transmission lines across the Panhandle and the Anadarko Basin need weld inspection during construction and corrosion monitoring in service. Pipeline welds usually follow API 1104, and operators apply federal pipeline safety rules and their own contractor requirements.

Refining. The refineries at Sunray and Borger bring steady inspection work and larger crews during turnarounds: UT thickness, MT and PT on repair welds, RT on new piping and VT throughout.

Wind energy. Construction and maintenance contractors inspect tower welds, flanges and bolting across the high plains.

Aerospace. Bell's Amarillo Assembly Center and its suppliers inspect structures and components to the prime's specifications and flow-down requirements.

Federal nuclear work. Pantex runs its own qualification programs under federal requirements and security clearance rules. Outside training is general background, not a route inside.

Agriculture, utilities and fabrication. Ammonia storage tanks, refrigeration systems at processing plants, utility generating stations and the fabrication shops that serve the oilfield all need weld and pressure-equipment inspection.

Employers usually ask for current method certifications, the written practice behind them, an experience log, a vision record and, for plant or pipeline work, site safety training. For pay information, see the NDT salary guide, which draws on public sources.

NDT schools and classes near Amarillo: what to compare

Amarillo is one of the few mid-size Texas cities with a dedicated college NDT program. Amarillo College runs a Nondestructive Testing and Evaluation program, with an associate degree and certificates covering visual, magnetic particle, penetrant, radiographic, ultrasonic and eddy current testing, and evening classes are offered. The college also has a welding program. For someone starting from scratch who wants lab time and a college credential, that is worth a close look.

Atlantis serves a different need: technicians already working, or sponsored by an employer, who want self-paced theory with Level III answers and a practical on the employer's own equipment. Whichever you consider, ask the same questions:

  • What do I leave with? A college credential or a training record is not SNT-TC-1A certification. The employer certifies, or ASNT does through central certification.
  • Does it match the written practice? Compare hours and content with what your employer requires.
  • Who teaches? Ask about ASNT Level III credentials in the methods covered.
  • How does the practical work? Find out where it happens and on what specimens.
  • Can it fit a travel schedule? Field technicians who rotate through jobs need study time that moves with them.
  • What support is included? Practice exams and access to an expert when you are stuck.

Online NDT training in Texas

From Amarillo, the nearest large metro areas are hours away by car, and a training trip to Dallas or Houston means hotel nights and lost work. Online theory keeps you at home or on the job. Atlantis courses run on the Atlantis portal year-round: enroll, get access straight away, and study from a motel room between field jobs if you need to, sending questions to an ASNT NDT Level III as they come up. Your employer's written practice decides how those hours count.

Rehearse practical skills in the Practical NDT browser simulator and take the graded practical in person at the employer's facility. See online NDT training, the Texas training page and the inland Texas page. Nearby city pages: Oklahoma City, Midland, Odessa, Albuquerque and Wichita.

Training a crew at your Amarillo facility (employers)

Panhandle inspection companies often have crews spread across several counties, which makes pulling everyone in for training expensive. A more practical plan:

  1. Check the written practice against the methods your crews perform and what pipeline, plant and aerospace clients require. See written practice development.
  2. Put theory online so technicians finish formal hours between jobs.
  3. Hold specific and practical examinations at your yard or shop, led by a Level III, on your procedures, equipment and representative specimens.
  4. Keep complete records for every technician: training, experience, examinations, vision and certification.
  5. Cover a missing Level III with ASNT Level III consulting.

Plan the onsite block for a quiet stretch between projects or ahead of turnaround season. Read about corporate NDT training and request an Amarillo crew training quote with your methods, levels and head-count.

Radiography licensing in Texas

Texas regulates radiation as an NRC Agreement State. The Radiation Control Program of the Texas Department of State Health Services licenses companies that perform industrial radiography, under rules in Title 25 of the Texas Administrative Code, including 25 TAC §289.255. Individual radiographers and radiographer trainees must meet state certification and training requirements, carry proof of certification on the job, and work in pairs at temporary field sites.

An RT course sits outside that system. It teaches exposure, image quality and interpretation, but it does not authorize anyone to use a source. Pipeline radiographers in the Panhandle therefore hold both the Texas radiographer qualification and an employer RT certification under SNT-TC-1A. Confirm current requirements with DSHS and your radiation safety officer.

Practice before your practical exam

Field technicians often know the work but freeze on exam day because the specimen, the instrument or the paperwork looks different from the job. Rehearse a full calibration, a thickness grid or weld scan and a complete report until the routine feels ordinary. Pipeline candidates should practice describing indications by location along the weld and position around the pipe.

The Practical NDT simulator offers virtual workplaces including an oil and gas site, a storage tank and a welding workshop, so you can rehearse setups and interpretation between theory modules. It builds habits; it does not replace logged experience or the graded practical on real specimens. For written drills, use the NDT practice tests.

Your instructor

Amarillo courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, with more than eleven years of field experience in several countries. The training catalog and the USA training page list all courses.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Amarillo

How do I become an NDT technician in Amarillo?

Learn visual and magnetic particle basics, apply to pipeline, plant or fabrication inspection companies that certify technicians, and complete Level 1 theory so an employer can sponsor your experience and examinations.

How long does NDT training take in the Texas Panhandle?

Level 1 theory for one method can be finished in days or a few weeks of self-paced study. Certification takes longer because experience hours have to be logged under supervision.

What does NDT training cost in Amarillo?

The table on this page shows the published US fees for standard courses, and Register & Buy Now opens each course on the Atlantis portal. Onsite crew programs are quoted separately.

Can I study NDT online in Texas?

Yes, for theory. The practical exam still happens hands-on, using real instruments and specimens at your employer's facility.

Is there an NDT school near me in Amarillo?

Atlantis NDT has no building in Amarillo. Amarillo College runs a college NDT program; Atlantis offers self-paced online theory with the practical at your employer's site.

Which NDT method should I learn first?

VT and MT first, then UT. Around Amarillo, UT thickness and weld examination are the skills employers ask for most often.

Are there NDT jobs in Amarillo?

Yes, mostly in pipeline construction and integrity work, gas plant and refinery inspection, wind tower inspection, aerospace manufacturing and fabrication. Many roles involve travel across the Panhandle.

Does my NDT certification move with me to a new employer?

Not automatically. The new employer reviews your records and certifies you under its own written practice; ASNT central certification stays with you.

Do radiographers need a Texas license?

Yes. The employer needs a DSHS radioactive material license, and each radiographer must hold Texas certification. An RT technique course alone does not meet that requirement.

Do you offer ASNT Level III preparation?

Yes. Panhandle candidates can prepare for the ASNT Basic and Method examinations online and at their own pace.
